Compensation $95,000 - $105,000 annually, based on experience and qualifications.

Position Summary The Senior Accountant is responsible for supporting the monthly close process, maintaining the integrity of financial records across multiple entities, overseeing inventory and cost accounting activities, and ensuring compliance with accounting standards and tax regulations. This role serves as a key partner to operations, finance leadership, and cross-functional teams while providing guidance to transactional accounting functions. Success in this role requires strong analytical skills, exceptional organization, the ability to manage competing priorities, and experience working within a manufacturing environment.

What You'll Do Financial Reporting & Month-End Close

Lead key month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close activities for multiple business entities. Prepare and review balance sheet reconciliations, accruals, prepaids, and intercompany transactions. Perform variance analysis and investigate financial discrepancies. Monitor balance sheet and profit & loss accounts to ensure accuracy and proper accounting treatment. Support external financial statement audits and banking audits.

Cost Accounting & Inventory Management

Maintain standard costing and inventory accounting processes within a manufacturing environment. Analyze inventory valuations, bill of materials (BOMs), labor absorption, and overhead costs. Coordinate physical inventories and cycle counts. Reconcile perpetual inventory records to the general ledger. Partner with operational teams to improve inventory accuracy and reporting.

Treasury & Cash Management

Support daily cash management and treasury activities. Review bank reconciliations and cash transactions. Investigate and resolve cash variances and reconciliation discrepancies.

Tax & Compliance

Manage multi-state sales and use tax compliance. Support business licenses, annual filings, and property tax reporting. Assist with federal and state tax credit documentation, including R&D-related activities. Support regulatory and audit requests.

Operational Support & Process Improvement

Collaborate with Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, and Payroll teams. Support credit review activities and monitor customer exposure. Identify opportunities to improve accounting processes and strengthen internal controls. Assist with reporting and financial activities across five operating entities.

What We're Looking For Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance. 4+ years of progressive accounting experience. Experience managing month-end close activities across multiple entities. Strong understanding of US GAAP and general ledger accounting. Manufacturing industry experience, including inventory and cost accounting. Advanced Microsoft Excel skills including pivot tables, lookups, and financial analysis. Proven ability to prioritize deadlines and manage multiple projects simultaneously. Strong communication skills and ability to work independently.

Preferred Qualifications

Public accounting experience. Experience transitioning from public accounting into corporate accounting. Familiarity with inventory modules and manufacturing ERP systems.

Experience with:

Epicor Kinetic Sage Intacct QuickBooks OneStream

Knowledge of multi-state sales tax compliance tools such as Avalara or Vertex. Construction or industrial manufacturing industry experience.

What Success Looks Like

In this role, you'll be trusted to:

Own critical aspects of the month-end close process. Manage accounting activities for multiple entities simultaneously. Understand what belongs in key balance sheet and P&L accounts and proactively monitor them. Meet deadlines with minimal oversight while knowing when to seek guidance. Communicate effectively with finance leadership and business partners. Bring a continuous improvement mindset to accounting processes and reporting.

Why Join Us?

Competitive compensation package Flexible work arrangement: remote, hybrid, or onsite Opportunity to work with a collaborative leadership team Exposure to multi-entity accounting and manufacturing operations Significant visibility within the finance organization Ability to make a meaningful impact on business performance and process improvements

Nous amorçons un virage stratégique vers les très grandes entreprises. Pour soutenir cette croissance, nous sommes à la recherche d'un(e) Spécialiste ABM – Entreprises (ABM Campaign Manager).

  • Alignement stratégique et ciblage : Collaborer avec notre GTM Engineer pour définir et prioriser la liste des comptes d'entreprise stratégiques, puis travailler au coude-à-coude avec les Account Executives (AE) pour concevoir des tactiques d'approche et faire progresser ces comptes.

Profil recherché

L’IA par réflexe

Nous sommes une équipe résolument tournée vers l’IA et nous cherchons un profil « IA-native». Nous utilisons l’IA autant en marketing qu'en vente, et nous souhaitons que cette personne pousse cette démarche encore plus loin dans notre façon d’exécuter l’ABM.

Ce que nous offrons

jobs.description:
Department: Finance

Reports To: Chief Financial Officer (CFO)

Employment Type: Full-Time

Work Arrangement: Remote

Work Schedule: 40 hours per week, Central Standard Time (CST)

Role Summary

Treantly is looking for an experienced and proactive Accounts Receivable Specialist to support one of our North American clients. The successful candidate will be responsible for managing the day-to-day accounts receivable process, including billing, invoicing, payment posting, and collections.

Collections will account for approximately 50% of the role, with a strong focus on proactively contacting customers, following up on outstanding invoices, resolving billing concerns, and securing timely payments.

We are looking for someone who is confident speaking with customers, persistent yet professional when following up on payments, and capable of investigating and resolving billing issues independently before escalating them.

Key Responsibilities

Collections and Customer Follow-Up (Approximately 50%)

  • Make proactive outbound collection calls daily to follow up on outstanding invoices and confirm payment timelines.
  • Contact customers shortly after larger invoices are issued to confirm receipt and address potential payment concerns before invoices become overdue.
  • Monitor accounts receivable aging reports and follow up on balances that are 30, 60, and 90+ days overdue.
  • Negotiate and document payment commitments, including agreed payment dates and amounts.
  • Send payment reminders, account statements, and follow-up emails to customers.
  • Investigate reasons for delayed payments, including billing discrepancies, pricing concerns, and invoice errors.
  • Respond to customer service tickets within two hours of receipt and minimize outstanding tickets.
  • Maintain accurate notes of customer interactions, payment commitments, and collection activities in ConnectWise.
  • Escalate complex billing disputes and seriously overdue accounts to the CFO with appropriate recommendations.
  • Maintain professional and positive customer relationships while ensuring timely collections.

Billing and Invoicing

  • Prepare and issue customer invoices accurately and on time using ConnectWise.
  • Verify invoice details, including pricing, quantities, applicable taxes, and billing requirements, by comparing customer quotes and system records.
  • Respond to customer inquiries regarding billing changes, invoice discrepancies, and payment concerns.
  • Investigate and troubleshoot billing issues independently before escalating them.
  • Prepare invoice adjustments, credit memos, and debit memos when required and approved.
  • Assist customers with payment portal access, including sending invitations and providing basic support.
  • Coordinate with internal team members to resolve billing-related concerns.

Payment Posting and Cash Application

  • Record and post customer payments in QuickBooks.
  • Match incoming payments to the correct customer accounts and outstanding invoices.
  • Investigate discrepancies involving partial payments, overpayments, and unapplied payments.
  • Assist with payment reconciliation and resolving outstanding customer balances.
  • Ensure payment records are accurate and updated promptly.

Accounts Receivable Management and Reporting

  • Review QuickBooks accounts receivable aging reports to identify overdue balances and prioritize collection activities.
  • Maintain accurate customer account records, billing information, and payment histories.
  • Track collection activities, outstanding balances, and customer payment commitments.
  • Prepare regular updates on collection progress, overdue accounts, and unresolved billing concerns.
  • Assist with accounts receivable reconciliations and month-end reporting as needed.
  • Coordinate closely with the CFO and relevant team members regarding billing and collection matters.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

Requirements

Qualifications and Requirements

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in accounts receivable, billing, invoicing, or collections.
  • Proven experience handling outbound collection calls and following up on overdue customer payments.
  • Excellent verbal and written English communication skills.
  • Confident and professional when communicating with North American customers over the phone.
  • Experience using QuickBooks or a similar accounting system.
  • Familiarity with accounts receivable aging reports, invoice processing, and payment posting.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate billing discrepancies and resolve customer concerns independently.
  • Comfortable handling high-value invoices and discussing outstanding balances with customers.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy when reviewing invoices, payment records, and customer accounts.
  • Excellent organizational and time-management skills.
  • Ability to work independently, prioritize collection activities, and meet deadlines.
  • Professional, persistent, and customer-focused approach to collections.
  • Ability to handle confidential financial and customer information responsibly.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience using ConnectWise for billing, invoicing, and customer account management.
  • Hands-on experience with QuickBooks accounts receivable reporting and payment processing.
  • Previous experience supporting U.S. or Canadian businesses.
  • Experience handling B2C collections and customer billing inquiries.
  • Familiarity with payment portals and automated billing systems.
  • Experience in the IT services or managed services industry.

Key Performance Expectations

  • Collections: Consistent daily follow-ups and reduction of overdue balances, particularly accounts over 60 and 90 days.
  • Customer Communication: Approximately 2–3 outbound collection calls daily, with timely email follow-ups and accurate documentation.
  • Proactive Follow-Up: Early communication with customers regarding high-value invoices to prevent payment delays.
  • Billing Accuracy: Invoices prepared and issued on time with minimal errors.
  • Payment Processing: Accurate and timely posting of customer payments.
  • Issue Resolution: Ability to independently resolve routine billing concerns while minimizing unnecessary escalations.
  • Customer Service: Respond to customer service tickets within two hours of receipt.

Tools and Systems

  • ConnectWise: Primary platform for billing, invoicing, customer communication records, and collection notes.
  • QuickBooks: Accounts receivable reporting, payment posting, and account monitoring.
  • Customer Payment Portal: Managing customer invitations and assisting with payment access.

Benefits

  • Opportunities for growth and advancement
  • Competitive compensation package, including Maxicare HMO

You will provide direction and training to CRAs assigned to the project under the guidance of the CTL. In addition, you may oversee of all operational aspects related to the planning and oversight of CRA and site performance, as delegated by the CTL. You will also help to ensure that sites and CRAs operate in compliance with study protocols, ICH/GCP guidelines, and Federal Regulations, in collaboration with the CTL.

What you’ll be doing:

Clinical Trial Operational Oversight

  • Provide support to CTLs in the end-to-end clinical execution of projects or programs, ensuring adherence to protocols, timelines, and regulatory requirements
  • Track and monitor recruitment, study metrics, monitoring, and documentation activities.
  • Demonstrate a proficient understanding of ICH-GCP and its practical application and ensure sites comply with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and applicable regulations
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams (e.g., data management, regulatory, safety) to facilitate study deliverables

Resource and Budget Management

  • Support the development and management of clinical operation timelines, metrics, resourcing, budget and activities
  • Contribute to risk identification and implementation of appropriate corrective actions and mitigation strategies
  • Support the tracking and reconciliation of clinical budgets related to clinical operation activities such as monitoring visits and CRA allocation

Stakeholder Communication

  • Support communication among Clients, site staff, and internal teams and proactively escalate issues to CTL and study team
  • Assist in preparing for and participating in internal and external meetings and managing routine Client communications

Team Leadership and Development

  • Assist with CRA and IHCRA project training, and onboarding and support preparation and delivery of training materials for investigator meetings, conferences, and team training
  • Foster collaboration across teams and ensures integration across project and sites
  • Provide constructive performance feedback on CRAs/IHCRAs to line managers and project leads
  • May participate in Bid Defense Meetings to present clinical operation and monitoring strategy

Quality Assurance & Compliance

  • Support protocol deviation review and reconciliation activities throughout the study by assisting with documentation, tracking, and coordination with cross-functional teams and Client for review and approval
  • Assist in identifying clinical risks and supports the implementation of mitigation strategies throughout the study
  • Assist with identifying, defining, documenting and ensuring compliance with project specific training requirements for clinical team

  • Bachelor's Degree, preferably in a life science, nursing, pharmacy or related field along with 3 years of clinical research experience within the CRO, pharmaceutical, or biotechnology industry and at least 2 years of on-site monitoring experience

About Us

At CoverGo, our mission is to empower all insurance companies to make insurance 100% digital and accessible to everyone.

  • We are a leading global no-code insurance platform for health, life, and P&C
  • We’re the winner of the Insurtech of the Year in all of Asia and other awards globally

About The Role

CoverGo is hiring an Application Security Engineer to use AI to find and prevent vulnerabilities before they reach production, and to give engineering teams the tools and guardrails that stop vulnerabilities from being introduced in the first place. The Security team is small and growing, and works AI-first: everyone uses AI to automate their own work and to scale security across a large engineering organisation.

What You Will Do

  • Use AI tools such as Claude and OpenAI models to find and triage vulnerabilities in code, dependencies and designs before changes are merged.
  • Embed security checks into developer workflows and CI/CD pipelines so issues surface as code is written.
  • Select, configure and tune code-security tools such as GitHub Advanced Security, Snyk and Checkmarx, keeping the signal high enough that engineers act on the findings.
  • Build self-service tools, guardrails and guidance that help engineering teams prevent common vulnerability classes.
  • Partner with engineering leads and security champions across product teams to prioritise and fix findings.
  • Review security-relevant designs and changes, ranking risk by what an attacker could realistically reach.
  • Track and report on application-security risk and remediation progress.

What We Need

  • 3+ years in application security or a closely related security role.
  • An AI-native approach to securing software: you already use LLMs to find, detect and explain vulnerabilities.
  • Enough fluency in at least one modern programming language to read, understand and fix vulnerable code. A software-engineering background is not required.
  • Hands-on experience with code-security tools such as GitHub Advanced Security, Snyk or Checkmarx.
  • A solid grasp of common vulnerability classes, such as the OWASP Top 10, and how to prevent them.
  • A practical, enabling style of working with engineers.

Nice to have

  • Experience building custom security tooling or automations on LLM APIs.
  • Experience securing applications on AWS, Azure or GCP.
  • Experience in insurance, financial services or another regulated SaaS environment.

Why You'll Love Working Here

  • Paid Annual Leaves
  • 13th-month Pay
  • Annual Performance Bonus
  • Health Insurance
  • Company activities and events

jobs.description:
Position: Estimator and Production Administrator

Salary: 1,900 AUD (Php 75,000 - 81,000)

Working Hours & Conditions: Monday to Friday AU Business Hours

ROLE OVERVIEW:

Approximately 75% of this role focuses on estimating, quotations and professional sales proposals, with the remaining 25% supporting production and business administration.

As a bespoke build company with an extensive hire inventory, we require someone who can confidently prepare and manage quotations combining date-based hire stock with custom fabrication and joinery builds for each project.

You will cost hired items against project dates and availability, while estimating bespoke components from designs, drawings, specifications, material quantities, fabrication methods and supplier pricing.

You will consolidate these elements into complete, accurate and commercially viable project quotations.Hands-on experience using software such as Rentman, Odoo, Current RMS, Booqable, HireHop, Tibr or a similar platform is essential.

You will work directly with our Designers to understand and cost each concept, and closely with our Producers, who manage client relationships and project delivery. You will report to the Producers and Managing Director.

About You

You are exceptional with numbers, highly organised and commercially aware. You enjoy translating a creative concept into a practical, accurate and clearly documented quotation.

You understand how hire inventory and custom-built components contribute to the total cost of delivering a project. You check quantities, rates, supplier pricing and margins carefully, and raise missing information or cost concerns early.

You are a proactive self-starter who can work independently, take ownership and follow tasks through to completion. You remain calm under pressure and manage competing priorities without compromising accuracy.

You take pride in getting the details right while working efficiently and meeting urgent deadlines.

Requirements

Estimating and Quotations – 75%

 Review client briefs, 3D designs, floor plans, construction drawings, specifications and finish schedules.

 Prepare detailed project estimates combining date-based hire inventory, bespoke fabrication, custom joinery, purchased materials and subcontracted services.

 Quote hire stock against delivery, installation, event, dismantling and return dates, accounting for hire duration, stock availability, turnaround time and external hire requirements.  Estimate custom-built joinery, display structures, signage, graphics and other fabricated components.

 Calculate material quantities, wastage, hardware, finishes, fabrication labour, assembly, freight, installation and dismantling costs.

 Obtain and compare quotations from fabricators, joiners, signage suppliers, installers, freight providers and other production partners.

 Check supplier quotations for scope completeness, quantities, exclusions, lead times and delivery requirements.

 Build and maintain quotations using item catalogues, hire rates, packages, supplier costs and project-specific fabrication estimates.

 Distinguish owned hire stock, externally hired equipment, purchased items and bespoke fabrication within internal cost breakdowns.

 Calculate selling prices, mark-ups and gross margins accurately.

 Work with Designers to assess buildability, material choices, fabrication methods and practical cost saving alternatives.

 Confirm project scope, budgets, inclusions, exclusions, assumptions and quotation deadlines with Producers.

 Prepare professional client quotations, sales proposals and tender submissions.

 Identify missing information, scope gaps, commercial risks and potential variations before quotations are issued.

 Manage quotation revisions as designs, quantities, dates and supplier costs change, checking their effect on availability, budgets and margins.

 Maintain current item catalogues, supplier rates, material pricing and estimating templates.  Review estimated costs against actual project costs to improve future pricing.

 Manage multiple quotations and urgent deadlines while maintaining accuracy.

Production and Office Administration – 25%

 Support Producers with purchasing, supplier coordination, project documentation, logistics and production administration.

 Prepare purchase orders and track supplier confirmations, lead times and delivery dates.

 Ensure approved materials, finishes, graphics, equipment and fabrication requirements are accurately ordered and documented.

 Maintain current project information as approved quotations move into production.

 Assist with hire schedules, equipment lists, packing lists and warehouse documentation.  Record approved changes and communicate updated information to Designers, Producers, suppliers and warehouse staff.

 Assist with freight bookings, deliveries, collections, installation and dismantling schedules.

 Organise supplier invoices and project cost records in Xero, checking them against purchase orders and approved costs.

 Maintain CRM records, supplier details, project folders and outstanding action lists.

 Provide regular updates on quotation progress, supplier pricing, project costs, deadlines and commercial risks.

 Communicate professionally with suppliers and contractors, while Producers retain primary responsibility for client management and project delivery.

Essential Skills and Experience

 Demonstrated experience estimating and quoting projects that combine date-based hire inventory with bespoke fabrication or custom joinery.

 Relevant experience in exhibitions, events, commercial joinery, shopfitting, signage, interior fit-outs or a comparable custom production environment.

 Hands-on experience using Rentman, Odoo, Current RMS, Booqable, HireHop, Tibr or a similar quotation, rental or business management platform.

 Practical experience using software to prepare quotations, maintain item catalogues and pricing, manage inventory information and track project costs.

 Ability to manage hire dates, stock availability, hire rates and external hire costs alongside project specific fabrication estimates.

 Advanced Microsoft Excel skills for estimating, calculations, pricing schedules and cost analysis.

 Practical experience using Xero for purchase orders, supplier invoices and project financial administration.

 Strong numerical skills, including a clear understanding of mark-up versus gross margin.

 Ability to interpret construction drawings, floor plans, specifications and 3D designs.

 Practical understanding of joinery and fabrication materials, construction methods, labour allowances, finishes and installation requirements.

 Experience obtaining and assessing supplier and subcontractor pricing.

 Ability to prepare professional quotations, proposals and clearly written scope descriptions.

 Excellent attention to detail, organisation and written and verbal communication.

 Demonstrated ability to work independently and complete accurate work within tight and changing deadlines.

Highly Regarded

 Direct experience in exhibition stand construction, event production or branded environments.

 Experience setting up or improving item catalogues, hire packages, pricing structures and quotation templates.

 Experience coordinating stock shortages, external hire, equipment substitutions and warehouse requirements.

 Experience tracking estimated versus actual costs and project profitability.  Familiarity with modular exhibition systems such as Octanorm, Maxima, Aluvision or beMatrix.

 Knowledge of timber and sheet materials, laminates, aluminium, steel, acrylic, signage, graphics, AV, lighting and flooring.

 Experience using CRM platforms and production scheduling software.

 Experience improving estimating processes and the handover from approved quotation to production.

Remote Working Requirements

 Ability to work independently and effectively in a full-time remote offshore role.

 Reliable internet access and a suitable workspace for focused estimating work and video meetings.

 Availability for agreed working hours that provide regular overlap with Colab’s Australian team.

 Confidence using online meetings, shared files and digital collaboration tools to work with Designers, Producers, suppliers and warehouse staff.

jobs.title: PPC Marketing Specialist
jobs.excerpt: Everyone can run a search campaign.  Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
jobs.description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Compliance, Governance & Quality - Patient Services
jobs.excerpt: The Executive Director, Compliance, Governance & Quality leads the enterprise programs that help PRO-spectus meet its obligations, establish clear accountability, and deliver consistent quality.
jobs.description:
The Executive Director, Compliance, Governance & Quality leads the enterprise programs that help PRO-spectus meet its obligations, establish clear accountability, and deliver consistent quality. As PRO-spectus's designated compliance lead, this leader builds and leads the compliance program, enterprise governance framework, and quality management program. The role establishes standards and controls, identifies risks and gaps, and drives corrective action across functions. Success means clear ownership, consistent adherence to requirements, and evidence that controls and improvements are effective.

This is a hands-on enterprise leadership role reporting to the Chief Innovation Officer (CINO). The Executive Director partners with the CINO to set strategy and priorities, personally leads program development and implementation, and may build a lean team as the programs mature. Working through functional partners, this leader puts standards into practice and provides senior leadership with clear reporting on risks, findings, and remediation. This role complements existing ownership. Functional leaders own execution and adherence within their areas, while People & Culture owns employee relations and disciplinary action.

Compliance Leadership

  • Build and lead the enterprise compliance program, including policies, monitoring, required training, and processes for identifying and addressing regulatory, contractual, and internal compliance requirements.
  • Form and chair the compliance committee, bringing together functional leaders to oversee compliance risks, the annual work plan, and remediation progress.
  • Conduct periodic compliance risk assessments and maintain a prioritized work plan, with clear owners, controls, and remediation deadlines for identified gaps.
  • Lead accreditation, regulatory, and client audit readiness and response, and represent PRO-spectus in quality reviews and compliance matters, in partnership with the Supervising Pharmacist and Pharmacy and Operations leaders, who retain ownership of pharmacy practice and licensure.
  • Partner with People & Culture, Training, and functional leaders to define compliance training requirements, monitor completion, and address gaps in understanding or adherence.
  • Establish processes for reporting compliance concerns, and lead or coordinate investigations and follow-up with People & Culture and legal counsel as needed.
  • Monitor relevant changes in requirements with subject matter experts, and coordinate updates to policies, controls, and procedures.
  • Resolve day-to-day compliance and governance matters independently and engage legal counsel with focused requests and a recommended approach when specialized expertise or material legal risk warrants review.

Enterprise Governance

  • Own the enterprise governance framework and policies, including document control, exceptions, and escalation; obtain executive approval where required and monitor adherence across functions.
  • Lead development of an enterprise decision-rights framework and RACI, securing executive approval and maintaining the framework as the organization evolves.
  • Build tools and processes that translate contractual commitments into clear owners, operational requirements, and documented procedures, and maintain a central view of obligations, status, and open gaps.
  • Own the full lifecycle of BAAs and NDAs, from intake through execution, renewal, and ongoing obligation management. Lead compliance review of MSAs, including negotiation of regulatory, privacy, data security, and related terms, and monitor compliance obligations after execution. Partner closely with the CFO, who serves as final reviewer and signatory, or a designated alternate.
  • Establish and maintain an enterprise calendar that gives leadership a single view of key obligations, commitments, and milestones across the organization, with a clear process for keeping it current and sharing it with the right audiences.
  • Require corrective action plans and status reporting from accountable owners; escalate overdue actions, significant risks, and unresolved concerns to the CINO and, when needed, the CEO or designated executive committee.
  • Provide regular executive reporting on compliance and governance risks, quality trends, open findings, and remediation progress, including periodic compliance reporting to the CEO and board through the CINO.

Document & Knowledge Governance

  • Own the lifecycle for SOPs, policies, and operational resources, including ownership, review cycles, approval, and change control, with authority to stop publication of documents that do not meet governance standards.
  • Chair the cross-functional SOP governance committee, facilitating review and decisions on material SOP changes and their potential operational, compliance, and client risk.
  • Establish the content governance model, including how content is organized, owned, named, and found, with a single authoritative source for every governed document.
  • Partner with Technology to build the enterprise knowledge and resource hub, with role-based access so employees can find what they need and sensitive content is appropriately restricted.
  • Partner with functional leaders and Training to ensure approved changes are communicated, trained, and adopted in daily operations.

Quality Management

  • Build and lead the enterprise quality management program, including baseline quality standards where client agreements do not define them, internal audits, and routine quality monitoring.
  • Partner with Operations and Pharmacy leaders to define quality measures and review whether procedures are followed and results meet established standards.
  • Establish deviation tracking, root cause analysis, and a corrective and preventive action (CAPA) process, with accountable owners and deadlines; verify that completed actions are effective.
  • Review trends across programs, identify recurring issues, and partner with functional leaders to implement improvements and monitor sustained results.

Skills & Requirements

  • Deep working knowledge of healthcare compliance and regulated operations (e.g., HIPAA, Anti-Kickback Statute, OIG guidance, state board of pharmacy requirements, URAC/ACHC accreditation).
  • Demonstrated ability to design and implement governance structures people actually use, including decision rights, RACI, document control, and escalation processes.
  • Demonstrated ability to make sound compliance and governance decisions independently and recognize when legal review is needed.
  • Working knowledge of quality management systems, including internal audit, root cause analysis, and CAPA.
  • Executive-level judgment and communication; leads through influence and holds leaders accountable for addressing compliance and governance gaps.
  • High degree of integrity, discretion, and confidentiality in handling sensitive matters.
  • Comfortable working remotely across U.S. time zones.
  • Project management experience preferred, including planning, milestone tracking, and status reporting.
  • Experience with Lean or Six Sigma process improvement methods preferred.

Education, Certifications & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business, quality, compliance, or a related field required; advanced degree preferred.
  • 12+ years of progressive experience in quality, compliance, regulated healthcare operations, or operational governance.
  • 5+ years of experience in compliance and governance required, including building or maturing compliance programs and implementing governance across functions.
  • Experience conducting compliance risk assessments, implementing controls, leading investigations and remediation, and building quality management processes preferred.
  • Experience in specialty pharmacy, patient services, hub services, or life sciences strongly preferred.
  • Experience leading accreditation, regulatory, or client audits strongly preferred.
  • Compliance certification preferred (e.g., CHC); quality or project management certifications are also valued (e.g., ASQ CQA, CPHQ, PMP).

Physical Requirements

As a remote-forward organization, this position operates in a virtual professional office environment and teleworking from the employee's home address listed in their employment file. Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer. Keyboarding, speaking, video conferencing, and sustained concentration. Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times. Flexibility of working hours to support activities across Eastern through Pacific time zones. Periodic travel may be required.

Our PRO-spectus Culture Philosophy

At PRO-spectus, we are fiercely dedicated to helping patients gain access to the care they need. Our team brings authenticity, compassion, humility, and urgency to the work of breaking down access barriers for patients, providers, and life sciences partners.

We believe meaningful impact happens when people work together with purpose. Our Market Access, Clinical Adherence, Pharmacy, Revenue Cycle Management, and Patient Support Services teams collaborate to optimize access, affordability, reimbursement, and patient experience. We are fearless in the face of complexity, agile in how we solve problems, and grounded in integrity as we support the patients and clients who depend on us.

All qualified individuals will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, protected veteran status, marital status, or other protected status under federal, state, or local laws.

At PRO-spectus, we are deeply committed to pay transparency and equity. The salary range for this position is $170,000 - 200,000, based on experience and qualifications, with the final offer reflecting skills and other job-related factors. Beyond competitive pay, we offer a comprehensive and generous benefits package designed to support your well-being and work-life balance.

Our benefits include robust medical, dental, and vision plans; life insurance and disability coverage; and tax-advantaged savings accounts. We also provide an Employee Assistance Program, home office benefits, and unique perks like an Employee Ownership Program. With paid time off, holidays, bereavement leave, and a 401(k)-retirement plan with employer matching, PRO-spectus prioritizes your financial and personal security. Forensic Regulatory Data Analyst – Utility Cost Recovery

UtiliSave's forensic billing analysts find actionable savings in 94% of the accounts they audit — including clients who were previously reviewed by another firm and believed nothing remained. If you have the instincts to absorb complex rules, spot the flaw no one else noticed, and relentlessly pursue a claim you know is right, you will thrive here.

Consider this: a large commercial building billed for peak electricity demand on the wrong interval meter. A university's water charges calculated under a rate code that hasn't applied to its account type for three years. A hospital's natural gas tariff with a weather normalization adjustment misapplied for 18 months. These are not hypotheticals — they are the types of claims our analysts have made, won, and been paid for. Join the team that has recovered over $700 million for large commercial and industrial clients across the U.S. and help us break through One Billion.

UtiliSave has been an industry leader in utility bill auditing services for over 35 years and is still growing rapidly. We are seeking curious, analytical action-takers with strong Python skills to join the team at the heart of our success — playing a key role in deep, forensic utility bill analysis for large commercial and industrial clients.

The core talent this role demands is the ability to rapidly absorb and master detailed billing rules, tariff schedules, demand charge structures, rider provisions, regulatory codes, and client usage data — and then deploy that knowledge creatively to find refunds and savings others miss. The ideal candidate thinks beyond established frameworks: constructing novel, sustainable claim theories that withstand regulatory scrutiny, and expressing those claims persuasively in writing and verbally to utilities, regulators, and clients.

On a typical day, you might write a Python script to flag demand charge anomalies across 40 accounts in the morning and draft a formal claim letter to a state utility commission in the afternoon. This is an ideal entry-level role for someone who wants to become an expert in a rare, financially consequential discipline and to see that expertise translates directly into personal earnings.

What You Will Build Here

UtiliSave is not a lateral move — it is a launchpad:

  • 3–6 months: Generating your first confirmed refund claims on live client accounts, guided by senior analysts and our proprietary platform.
  • 12–18 months: Independently managing a portfolio across multiple utility jurisdictions with a growing track record of recoveries.
  • 24+ months: High performers advance to Senior Analyst, Practice Lead, or Client Relationship Manager — with expanded compensation and client ownership.

The expertise you build here — utility tariff law, regulatory billing, forensic financial analysis — is rare and directly monetizable. Few entry-level roles put this much earning power in your own hands this quickly.To apply, email your resume and optional cover letter to with the job title in the subject line. jobs.excerpt: Liquid Instruments builds test and measurement tools for engineers and scientists who need precise, flexible instruments.
jobs.description:
Liquid Instruments builds test and measurement tools for engineers and scientists who need precise, flexible instruments. Our founders are scientists from the Australian National University and NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. Our work in high-speed digital signal processing and ultra-sensitive instruments began with technology built to measure gravitational waves.

Our main product line, Moku, is a reconfigurable and reprogrammable, FPGA-based test and measurement platform. It handles both simple measurements and complex setups that use many instruments at once, and it is fast and straightforward to customize. Moku pairs capable hardware with easy-to-use software to balance flexibility, performance, and cost.

Liquid Instruments is headquartered in Canberra, Australia, with a U.S. office in Del Mar (San Diego), California.

Why this role exists

Moku fits two defense priorities: electromagnetic spectrum operations (EMSO) and assured positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT).

In electronic warfare (EW) and EMSO, threats change faster than test infrastructure. Conventional test benches are built from racks of separate instruments and chassis-based systems. Each one is specified, integrated, and maintained on its own. Moku combines that stack into a single software-defined unit. Signal capture and analysis, threat waveform generation, real-time DSP, and spectrum monitoring run on one platform that reconfigures in software as requirements change. It is the modern architecture for EW test: faster to deploy, easier to scale, and built to evolve with the threat.

In PNT, the move toward GPS-denied and alternative navigation depends on precision timing, phase measurement, and ultra-low-noise control. Our instruments come from that same work. It also connects directly to quantum inertial sensing as those sensors move into fielded systems.

Moku is already established in precision optics and photonics labs worldwide. This role leads our expansion into EW/EMSO and PNT. You'll set the programs and customers we prioritize, the applications we lead with, and how we win them.

You'll be our technical authority on A&D. You'll define where we compete. Sales will bring you into hard calls, and R&D will ask you what the market needs. You'll write the technical work that earns Moku's credibility with defense engineers.

San Diego preferred; U.S. remote considered.

Your work will include

Market strategy and segmentation. You'll define the EW/EMSO and PNT segments and applications where Liquid Instruments leads. You'll support Product Management in sizing the dollar opportunity in each segment so we invest where the return is greatest. You'll map how primes, neo-primes, defense research labs, FFRDCs, and SBIR and venture-backed companies buy, and assess how programs of record, ITAR and export control, and NDAA supply chain rules shape our path to market, including how our Australian presence positions us under AUKUS Pillar 2. You'll bring leadership a clear recommendation backed by evidence.

Competitive analysis. You'll support Product Management in tracking competitors' products, pricing, positioning, and roadmaps. You'll turn that analysis into deal-level guidance on where Moku wins and into sharper messaging, treating what competitors build as a signal of what customers are asking for.

Messaging. You’ll own vertical and product-level messaging for A&D, built on our existing company messaging framework. You’ll validate it with defense engineers. And ensure Marketing and Sales use it consistently.

Technical proof. You’ll write application notes, white papers, and benchmark data that establish Liquid Instruments in defense labs. Topics include wideband signal capture and analysis, threat waveform generation, real-time DSP, spectrum monitoring, phase and timing measurement, and clock characterization for assured PNT.

Launch and go-to-market. You’ll own the technical go-to-market for new A&D products, from positioning to sales enablement to launch content.

Sales enablement. You’ll build the training content, competitive battlecards, and demos ffor our Sales team, application engineers, and channel partners. The goal is for them to lead a credible conversation with a defense lab, prime, or neo-prime. You’ll support strategic pursuits hand in hand with our Sales team.

Influence on the roadmap. You’ll bring organized evidence from defense customers to Product Management and R&D. You’ll make the case for the capabilities, performance, environmental, and compliance requirements this market needs.

Technical presence. You'll work with customer engineering teams and programs to support evaluations, give demos, and lead technical sessions. You'll represent Liquid Instruments at key events and publish and present as part of the role. Expect about 30% travel.

You'll work closely with the Content, Field Marketing, and Design teams. They own the blog calendar, social channels, website production, and event logistics.

  • You've delivered an A&D segmentation and priority strategy that Marketing, Sales, and Product use to guide investment. It includes a clear path through export control and procurement requirements
  • Vertical and product messaging is tested with defense engineers, distinct from competitors, and in use across Marketing and Sales
  • You've published at least four application notes, white papers, case studies, or benchmark studies. Defense engineers find them on their own, and Sales cites them
  • Sales teams run your demos and handle defense conversations without you on the call
  • Sales uses the competitive insight you've developed with Product Management to position Moku in active deals

  • You've owned the technical go-to-market for at least one product launch

Requirements

  • 8+ years in product marketing, product management, business development, solutions architecture, applications engineering, systems engineering, or another customer-facing technical role, with substantial time in or near aerospace and defense
  • Proven depth in electronic warfare, EMSO, SIGINT, radar, or assured PNT: the applications, test and validation workflows, programs, and key players
  • Hands-on familiarity with RF and wideband test and measurement equipment: spectrum analyzers, signal generators, oscilloscopes, digitizers, and FPGA-based signal processing
  • Working understanding of defense procurement: primes, neo-primes, and subs; programs of record; SBIR/STTR; and how test equipment decisions are made
  • Familiarity with ITAR, EAR, and defense supply chain requirements
  • [U.S. person status required. Active or prior security clearance, or eligibility to obtain one, preferred.]
  • Experience supporting market sizing and competitive analysis
  • Understanding of competitors, including Keysight, NI, Rohde & Schwarz, Tektronix, Safran, and precision timing vendors, plus the PXI and open-architecture ecosystem
  • A track record of bringing a technical product into a defense market, from strategy through execution
  • Able to lead work across teams without formal authority
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and fast-moving work
  • Travel for industry events and customer engagements (30%)

jobs.title: Senior Frontend Engineer
jobs.excerpt: About vidIQvidIQ builds software to help YouTube creators achieve their goals.
jobs.description:
About vidIQ

vidIQ builds software to help YouTube creators achieve their goals. Our mission is to advance the creator's journey with actionable data-driven insights and AI-powered tools. We are dedicated to our values of being creator-obsessed, lean and fast, and scientific. Having already supported millions of creators, we invite stunning new co-workers to join us in reaching millions more.

Imagine a product that reached over a million users without a traditional sales team. This product stands at the forefront of career evolution, where everyone can be their own brand with unlimited growth potential. That's the opportunity at vidIQ—an infinite market, a large and highly engaged customer base, and the chance to help scale the platform that delivers insights to millions of creators.

Discover more about vidIQ firsthand at www.vidiq.com.

About the Team

Our vision is to build a personal copilot for every YouTube creator. We work in small, focused teams where people are expected to understand the problem, make decisions, and take ownership of the outcome.

We value people who are strong in their craft, communicate clearly, challenge ideas with respect, and follow through from problem to production.

We’re also an AI-native team. We build AI into our product and use it every day in how we work—from writing and reviewing code to debugging, testing, prototyping, and exploring new ideas.

About the role

vidIQ meets creators where they are, through a web app, mobile apps, and browser extensions. Our frontend is built with React, Next.js, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind. We use a range of AI models to power creator-facing features such as ideation, metadata generation, and content insights.

This is a frontend-leaning role, but you won't stop at the frontend. You'll own entire product surfaces from end to end: the UI, the APIs behind it, the data it depends on, and how it performs in production. We expect you to understand the problem, decide what to build, and ship it.

You'll shape how millions of creators experience vidIQ, and you'll help define how our engineering team builds software now that AI is a real collaborator.

This is a remote position open to candidates worldwide. Employment classification and engagement structure will be determined based on location, legal requirements, and mutual fit.

What you will do:

  • Own product surfaces end to end. You'll be the go-to owner for key parts of vidIQ, we serve over 1M daily active creators. You'll set their direction, track how they perform, and decide what to improve next.

  • Work across the stack. You'll build and change backend APIs, services, and data flows when a feature needs it, instead of waiting on another team.

  • Drive your own roadmap. You'll spot opportunities in user feedback, data, and the codebase, turn them into proposals, align with product and design, and deliver without needing to be managed closely.

  • Modernize the frontend. You'll lead the refactor of key features from JavaScript to TypeScript to improve performance and maintainability, using AI-assisted tooling where it speeds up the work without lowering the bar for quality.

  • Build AI-powered product experiences. You'll ship LLM-driven features across the stack, from model integration and prompts on the backend to streaming responses, error handling, and clear UX when model output is unpredictable.

  • Fix architecture and performance problems. You'll find bottlenecks and weaknesses anywhere in the request path, frontend or backend, and leave the system better than you found it.

  • Make AI part of how the team works. You'll use tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot every day, share what works, and help set team practices for using AI responsibly.

  • Improve durability. You'll test important workflows, add useful monitoring and error reporting, and own what you ship after it's live, whether you wrote every line or reviewed and refined AI-generated code.

  • Raise the bar through review and mentorship. You'll review code from other engineers, AI-assisted or not, and give feedback that helps others grow.

Requirements

  • About You

    • You have at least 5 years of professional software development experience.

    • You're strongest on the frontend, but you're comfortable on the backend. You can design an API, write server-side code, work with databases, and debug problems that cross the client-server boundary.

    • You're self-driven. You don't need a detailed spec to get started, and you're happy making decisions, asking the right questions, and moving work forward on your own.

    • You act like an owner. When something you're responsible for breaks, underperforms, or confuses users, you notice and fix it before anyone asks.

    • You've led projects from concept to completion, including documenting the work and teaching others about it.

    • You care about product quality and leave codebases in better shape than you found them.

    • You write and speak clearly, and you can explain technical concepts to non-technical people.

    • You're confident with TypeScript, React, Next.js, Vite, and Tailwind.

    • You're a heavy, thoughtful user of AI tools. AI coding assistants and agents are part of how you plan, build, debug, test, and review every day. You know where they save you hours and where they fail, and you check AI output as carefully as you'd check a teammate's pull request.

    • You keep up with the fast-moving AI landscape and like trying new models, tools, and workflows.

Nice to have

  • Backend experience with , Scala, and/or Python, plus relational databases, caching, and queues

  • Experience with Redux, Redux Saga, and/or Zustand

  • Experience building LLM-powered features, such as streaming UIs, model APIs, prompt design, or evals

  • Experience with agentic coding workflows, such as running AI agents on multi-step tasks, writing custom rules or context files, or using MCP servers

Perks and Benefits

  • Work Remotely: Embrace the freedom to choose your ideal workspace anywhere in the world.

  • Flexible Time Off: We support a flexible vacation policy allowing you to take time off when you need to recharge.

  • Communication Stipend: Enjoy a monthly stipend to cover your phone and internet expenses, helping you stay connected effortlessly.

  • Global Impact: Join our diverse team that’s shaping the future of the creator economy across the globe.

  • Competitive Compensation: vidIQ believes in offering competitive compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and contributions. We ensure fairness through internal equity and geo-location based pay, with the upper range reserved for individuals demonstrating exceptional job knowledge and skills.

Our Commitment

At vidIQ, we dedicate ourselves to enabling creators of all kinds to succeed. We prioritize attracting diverse talent and fostering an environment that encourages collaboration, creativity, and personal growth. We are committed to building a company and a community where individuals thrive by being true to themselves and are inspired to do their best work every day.

If you share our enthusiasm for empowering creators, we would love to hear from you. Click the “Apply” button below to start your journey with us.

The Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition (CFSAN) is the branch of the United States Food and Drug Administration that regulates food, dietary supplements, cosmetics, drugs, biologics, medical devices, and radiological products.
  • The scope of this contract is to provide the full range of technical and management services necessary to develop, maintain, and enhance CFSAN systems. The general requirements include providing Custom Computer Programming Services (NAICS 541511) to the FDA and CFSAN; and to maintain, support, and evolve code, scripts, views, triggers, jobs, designs, documentation, reports, and templates.
  • There is also a need to establish an ordering vehicle that develops and maintains existing and future Computer to Plate (CTP) systems, which will process structured and unstructured data. The FDA expects between 2-5 new applications/systems to be added to the BPA per year over the duration of this contract. The ProSidian Engagement Team shall provide training services to CFSAN stakeholders for existing applications, application changes, or newly-developed applications. CFSAN will issue individual Task Orders for the Contractor to provide IT Lifecycle Support for the CFSAN IT portfolio of systems as needed. Representative tasks to be performed.

THE BLANKET PURCHASE AGREEMENT IS DIVIDED INTO THE FOLLOWING (9) TASK AREAS:

  • Task 1: Project Management: Task Order level project management to establish control, management, monitoring and notification mechanisms to ensure the individual task orders stay on track to meet the important milestones and performance measures within the awarded task. | DOCUMENTATION: The Contractor shall use FDA supplied templates which will be provided on each individual Task Order as applicable. If an FDA template does not exist, the Contractor may be tasked with drafting a template for approval by the COR.
  • Task 2: O&M and DME Architecture Support Services: The Contractor shall provide the full range of architecture support services in order to formulate the integrated, end-to-end automated systems that provide enhanced IT capabilities necessary to support CFSAN business and mission processes. The goal is a stable evolutionary progression from an organization’s current state to its envisioned future state by identifying tools and technologies that work together to satisfy the needs or changing business needs of the CFSAN users.
  • Task 3: Development, Modernization, and Major Enhancement: The Contractor shall provide the complete range of system development lifecycle support services necessary to develop and enhance CFSAN IT systems and tools as well as their external interfaces to FDA Enterprise and Center Systems and applications. Tasks may encompass the complete lifecycle of activities required for database, application and tool development including, but not limited to requirements elicitation, analysis and validation; system design; code generation; testing; deployment; and documentation. The Contractor shall also develop, support and evolve designs, customizations and process automation such as interfaces, templates, scripts, workflows, interfaces to permit reviewer access to analytics/tools, and reports. Deliverable products shall be validated and tested to ensure that they meet applicable/specified standards, policy, business requirements.
  • Task 4: Systems Integration and Engineering Services: The Contractor shall support CFSAN with integration services. The Contractor shall focus on the development and deployment of integrated information systems that reflect the introduction of a Service Oriented Architecture (SOA) orientation and, moreover, places an emphasis on the recommended acquisition and re-use of existing components—be they FDA components, HHS components, or components acquired from any other source.
  • Task 5: Data Migration and Management Support: The Contractor shall provide data management support for activities related to the development and execution of data architectures, data policies, practices, and procedures that properly manage the full data lifecycle needs of CFSAN. Task #6 - Operations and Maintenance (O&M) and Support Services
  • Task 6: Operations and Maintenance (O&M) and Support Services: The Contractor shall provide the complete range of operations and maintenance support services necessary to maintain CFSAN IT systems. The Contractor shall be responsible for maintaining the “lights on” availability, reliability, and security of the CFSAN IT portfolio through the full range of O&M services. The Contractor shall maintain, support, and evolve code, scripts, views, triggers, jobs, designs, documentation, reports, and templates. The Contractor shall analyze and report on the impact of infrastructure, software upgrades, capacity, and all changes to the technical environment. These day-to-day operations, maintenance, and help desk support ensures that the systems perform their intended functions.
  • Task 7: System and Data Disposition: The Contractor shall identify, recommend and implement the retirement and consolidation of systems, components, technologies, tools and data when they meet the appropriate disposition stage of the lifecycle as defined in the EPLC.
  • Task 8: Training Support for O&M and DME: The Contractor shall provide training services to CFSAN stakeholders for existing applications, application changes, or newly developed applications. The Contractor shall assess the level of capability of the users and the need for training. The Contractor shall prepare a training plan, the training materials, and arrange and conduct training sessions. The training plan and materials shall be provided to the COR for review and approval prior to training.
  • Task 9: Transition Activities: The Contractor shall provide the transition-in and transition-out of activities to develop, operate, and manage the CFSAN IT portfolio. It is the responsibility of both the incoming Contractor and outgoing Contractor to ensure a smooth transition, with minimal disruption to services and support for users. The purpose of the transition is to transfer expert knowledge, data, and artifacts that are used to support applications from the incumbent Contractor to the successor Contractor efficiently.

*** Enterprise Performance Lifecycle (EPLC) Agile Methodology: The Food and Drug Administration maintains a project management methodology framework that incorporates best government and commercial practices through a consistent and repeatable process, and provides a standard structure for planning, managing and overseeing IT projects over their entire life cycle. The HHS Enterprise Performance Life Cycle (EPLC) framework provides that methodology for HHS OPDIVs including FDA.

jobs.title: Remote Clinical Psychologist - Massachussetts
jobs.excerpt: Prosper Health is on a mission to make life happier and healthier for autistic and neurodivergent adults.
jobs.description:
Prosper Health is on a mission to make life happier and healthier for autistic and neurodivergent adults.

Despite autism diagnoses increasing more than 5x in the past 25 years, autistic adults have been systematically overlooked. This has led to extremely poor outcomes, including high rates of co-occurring mental health conditions and a lower life expectancy. Prosper is here to change that.

We deliver specialized mental health services for autistic adults, covered by insurance. We've helped tens of thousands of people receive an autism diagnosis for the first time, work with neurodivergent-affirming therapists, and find belonging through community. Our outcomes meaningfully outperform traditional care for autistic adults, with substantially greater improvements in mood, anxiety, and quality of life.

Prosper is growing 3x year over year and are at mid-double-digit millions in run-rate revenue, with thousands of active clients and 400+ clinicians. We're a high-ownership, mission-driven team, building something that has never existed for autistic and neurodivergent adults.

The Role

We're hiring Licensed Psychologists (Ph.D/Psy.D) to conduct autism assessments for adults via telehealth. You'll join a team dedicated to creating affordable, accessible diagnostic services while helping to shape best practices in adult autism assessment.

Our clinicians come from diverse backgrounds and career stages - whether you're building your career foundation, balancing work with other responsibilities, or expanding your clinical expertise, we offer flexibility to match your needs.

What You'll Do

  • Conduct comprehensive autism assessments for adults via telehealth
  • Deliver actionable feedback to clients following evaluations and develop personalized post-assessment plans
  • Write clear, thorough clinical reports that document findings and recommendations
  • Participate in case consultations and clinical collaborative opportunities
  • Focus on direct client care while we handle administrative tasks and insurance billing

What We Offer

Flexible Work Options:

  • Schedule autonomy (7am-10pm - 7days a week)
  • Part-time/Contract roles start at just 18 hours per week
  • Full-Time salaried positions available with benefits
  • Work from your private office or space, regardless of geographic location

Clinical Support Structure:

  • Administrative support including scheduling, billing and insurance done for you, not by you so you can focus on clinical work
  • Purpose-built technology for effective telehealth assessment and report writing
  • Paid, structured onboarding program - we will set you up for success no matter your level of experience with Autism
  • Inclusive, neurodiversity-affirming community of clinicians that values diverse perspectives and collaborative growth

Professional Development:

  • Regular case consultation groups and monthly case conferences in a Project ECHO format
  • Mentorship opportunities with experienced clinicians while you acclimate to our processes and systems
  • Clear career advancement opportunities with pathways to lead roles and clinical leadership positions

Benefits (Full-time Positions):

  • Comprehensive Medical/Dental/Vision coverage
  • 401(k) retirement plan
  • 15 days PTO plus major holidays

What We Look For:

Required Qualifications:

  • Doctoral degree (PhD/PsyD) from an APA-accredited program
  • Current state licensure as a Licensed Psychologist with no disciplinary actions
  • Identity-affirming approach to patient care
  • Strong clinical judgment and clinical interview skills
  • Proficient remote communication abilities
  • Tech competence and self-direction
  • Desire to support an underserved population of autistic adults

Preferred Qualifications:

  • PSYPACT licensure or eligibility
  • Experience with adult diagnostic evaluations
  • Background working with neurodivergent populations

Join Our Team

Ready to transform lives while advancing your career? Apply today to join Prosper Health's team of dedicated professionals making a real difference for autistic and neurodivergent adults.

Prosper Health is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, including those who identify as neurodivergent, LGBTQ+, or BIPOC.

For those interested in 1099 opportunities, we offer a per assessment rate, paid upon submission of the assessment.

Weekly pay
$1,650—$2,200 USD

We also offer salaried roles that come with full benefits.

Annual Salary Range
$100,000—$120,000 USD

More about Prosper Health

  • Our culture is a unique mix of thoughtfulness, kindess, and high-performance. We set ambitious goals and hold ourselves accountable to achieving them.
  • We always ensure that we integrate perspectives from experts in our space, including clinicians and autistic self-advocates.
  • Our team members come from places such as Bain, McKinsey, BCG, FirstHand Health, Rula, SeatGeek, Benchling, and schools like Harvard, MIT, Stanford, Yale, Penn, Dartmouth, Northwestern, Vanderbilt, and more.
  • Here are a few of our favorite operating principles:
    • Clients first - Our job is to solve real problems for our clients. Choose what makes life better for the client, even if it’s harder for us. Never lose sight of the person on the other side.
    • Find a Way - We use ingenuity, scrappiness, and determination to bend the world to accomplish our goals. We’re resourceful and do more with less.
    • Raise the Bar - We grow deliberately, by asking how things can improve and by giving and seeking feedback. We insist on the highest standards and keep pushing them higher.
    • Be a Good Person - Be kind, be honest, and make it fun to work here. Tell the truth even when it’s uncomfortable. Treat people with respect and go out of your way to do nice things for your teammates.
